newsitem.title: LATVIA: MPS VOTE ON SECURITIES BOARD POSTS NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: MPS VOTE ON SECURITIES BOARD POSTS NEXT WEEK.

text.p: Latvia's parliament will vote on the remaining three securities commission board posts next week with the party faction failing to come to a unanimous opinion on the candidates on Wednesday, politicians said.

"No agreement was reached on the three candidates by the faction's coopeartion council today and the MPs will have to make a final decision," Andrejs Pantelejevs, head of the Latvia's Way faction, told Reuters.
Parliament is expected to vote on the issue either next Wednesday or Thursday, the spokeswoman for the parliamentary budget commission said.
The parliament budget committee meeting today supported only one of the three, Janis Brazovskis, currently deputy head of the central bank's department of credit institution supervision, she said.

The other candidates suggested by Viktors Gustsons, the chairman of the commission, are Andris Miglavs, acting manager of the State Agrarian Policy Institute, and Pauls Dzintars Kalninsh, co-owner of the U.S. based consultancy Baltic Ventures Inc.
The securities commission had four of its planned seven board members approved by parliament earlier this month, making it capable of decision making.
